transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess I'm having some trouble in the evenings. After work. I try to be pretty strict during the day, but then... I don't know, I just end up eating way more than I meant to. 

Like... I'll have dinner, and then maybe some cereal, or crackers, whatever leftovers are around... sweets. Just... all within a couple of hours. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started, even if you want to?

Yeah... I suppose so. Once I get started on those nights, it's like... I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm telling myself to stop, I just... I don't. I don't really feel back in charge until I'm... well, until I'm uncomfortably full.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating?
Um... yeah, I suppose so. I don't really like to dwell on it, though. I just... try to go to sleep after.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during those episodes?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid much attention to that. I don't think I'm rushing, exactly... just eating.
Do you feel like you're eating in secret during those episodes, or hiding the fact that you're eating from others?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I'm usually just by myself anyway when it happens. So... I don't think I'm purposely hiding anything.
Do you feel like you're in control of what or how much you're eating during those episodes?

Um... I guess not really. It's just... once I get started on those nights, I kind of keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm telling myself to stop, I just don't. I don't really feel back in charge of it until I'm just... uncomfortably full.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these episodes of eating?
Um... no, I don't think so. It pretty much just stays the same, I guess. I haven't really noticed any big changes.
Do you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes in the evenings, after work... especially if I've been trying to be strict during the day. I just end up eating... a lot more than I meant to. Like, I'll have dinner, and then... maybe cereal, some crackers, leftovers, sweets... all within a couple of hours, I suppose.
Do you feel like you're able to choose what you eat during those episodes or do you feel like you're not really making choices?

Um... I think I already mentioned this, but... no, I don't really feel like I'm making choices. Like I said before, once I start, I just keep going back for more. I tell myself to stop, but I just don't. I'm not really back in charge until I'm... well, until I'm too full.
Do you feel like you're able to control how much you're eating during those episodes?

Um... well, like I just said... no. I don't really control the amount either. Once I get started on those nights, I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm telling myself to stop... I just don't. I don't really feel back in charge until I'm... uncomfortably full.
How often do these episodes of eating more than you meant to happen?

Um... I guess for the past few months, it's been happening... most weeks. Usually just one or two nights a week. I just eat way more than I meant to, and then... well, the next day I try to fix it. I'll skip meals, or... maybe stay on the treadmill a lot longer than usual. Just to make up for it, I guess.
How often do you try to make up for the extra food you ate by skipping meals or exercising more?

Um... well, like I just said, it's... it's about the same. If I have one of those nights, the next day is when I try to fix it. So... yeah, for the past few months, it's most weeks. One or two times a week I'll... skip eating or stay on the treadmill. Just depends on how many times I messed up the night before.
Have you ever used any methods to try to purge the food you ate during those episodes, such as vomiting or laxatives?
Um... no. I don't... I've never done anything like that. Just the things I already mentioned.
Do you experience any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to these episodes of eating?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean... I still go to work. I'm an insurance agent, so I have clients to keep up with, and... I still do that. And I help mentor some of the newer agents. I still do everything I need to do at home, too. It's just... sometimes, I guess... if I have a public event or something, I might feel a little... distracted. Or just... less confident, I suppose, if I'm worrying about how my clothes are fitting that day. But... I still do my job.
How many times a month would you say you have one of these episodes where you eat more than you meant to?

Um... well, I think I mentioned a minute ago... it happens most weeks. Usually one or two nights a week where I eat way more than I meant to. So... I guess maybe six or eight times a month? It's been like that for the past few months. And then... yeah, like I said, the next day is when I try to make up for it by skipping a meal or exercising. I don't keep an exact count, but... that's probably close.
How many days a week do you try to make up for the extra food you ate by skipping meals or exercising more?

Um... well, like I just said... it's usually the day after. So... if I overeat one or two nights a week, then... I guess it's one or two days a week that I skip meals or... stay on the treadmill longer. It just matches up with whenever the eating happens.
Do you try to make up for the extra food you ate on the same day it happens, or is it usually the next day?

Um... yeah, like I said, it's usually the next day. After one of those nights, I just... I tell myself I need to make up for it. So I'll skip breakfast and lunch... or maybe take an extra-long hike. Sometimes I'll just push a lot harder at softball conditioning, even if I'm really tired. But... yeah, it's the next day.
Do you think your eating habits are significantly impacting your daily life or overall well-being?

Um... I wouldn't say significantly. I'm still keeping up with my clients and... my mentoring role at work. Everything at home gets done. I guess... sometimes I just get a little distracted. Or... maybe less confident if I have to go to a public event for work. Just... if I'm worrying about how my clothes are fitting. But... I still do what I need to do.
Do these episodes of eating more than you meant to, followed by trying to make up for it, happen at least once a week for the past three months?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. For the past few months, it's been... well, most weeks. Like I said, one or two nights I end up eating way more than I meant to, and... then the next day I do what I have to do to make up for it. So, yes.
Have these episodes of eating more than you meant to, followed by trying to make up for it, happened at least once a week for the past three months?
Um... I think I just answered that. But... yes. Like I said, it's most weeks.
